NKE.rationale: NKE is experiencing severe, accelerating fundamental deterioration across all key metrics. EPS has declined four of the last five quarters, reaching $0.35 in Q3 FY2026 (−35.2% YoY). Gross margin has compressed from 43.6% to 40.2%, operating margin collapsed from 11.5% to 5.8%, and operating cash flow fell 76% YoY to $430M — below net income of $520M, signaling broken cash conversion. ROE has halved from 32.2% to 16.0%. At 29× trailing PE, the stock's 3.4% earnings yield sits below the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.4%, meaning the market is pricing in a recovery that the data does not support. The macro backdrop is hostile: WTI crude has surged 76% to $108.64, creating dual margin and demand headwinds for a discretionary consumer brand already under cost pressure from tariffs (300 bps hit in North America). While the qual report highlights early turnaround signals (North America wholesale +11%, NIKE Running +20%) and the FIFA World Cup 2026 as a catalyst, the quant data shows no margin inflection — Q4 guidance calls for revenue declines of 2-4% and Greater China revenues to fall ~20%. The turnaround is explicitly 'early stage' and non-linear, while the earnings trajectory is accelerating downward. P/B at 4.665× (floor of 365d range) appears cheap but is structurally justified by halved ROE. All three pillars align negatively: (1) deteriorating fundamentals with no visible inflection, (2) valuation that embeds unsupported recovery expectations, and (3) no credible near-term fundamental catalyst that could re-rate the stock before the earnings trajectory stabilizes. The World Cup is H2 2026 at earliest and cannot offset the current margin/cost crisis.

P/E diluted 29.2× with earnings yield 3.4% below 10Y Treasury yield of 4.4% — market pricing recovery not supported by data
WTI crude surged 76% to $108.64, creating input cost and consumer demand headwinds for discretionary brand
Tariffs imposed 300 bps gross margin headwind in North America; management expects tariff headwinds to persist into Q1 FY2027
Q4 FY2026 guidance: revenue decline 2-4%, Greater China revenues projected to fall ~20% — no near-term inflection
Turnaround under CEO Elliott Hill showing early North America wholesale traction (+11%) but explicitly 'early stage' with non-linear path
Competitive erosion from Hoka (~10% US performance running share) and On (~9%) as Nike's share slipped to ~25%
